headline: Approved $29,500 police chief search contract; council employee evaluation change passed 7-1; corruption investigation resolution held to next meeting.
summary: Residents spoke about the Arlington neighborhood sewer project, delayed school contracts, and a resolution on reopening a corruption investigation. The council approved a police chief search contract and a change to council employee evaluations. A motion to table the corruption resolution failed 4-4, so it moves to the next regular meeting.
decisions: Approved appointment of Marilyn Murphey to the Council of Aging, unanimously.
Approved a $29,500 contract with Blue Integrity Consulting to search for a new police chief, unanimously.
Approved amendment to the annual performance evaluation for City Council employees, 7-1.
Motion to table the resolution calling for reopening the federal corruption investigation failed 4-4, so the resolution moves to the next regular meeting.
Approved acceptance of a gift of 9/11 Memorial banners, unanimously.
Approved ordinance adding the sealer of weights and measures position to the pay plan, unanimously.
Referred open meeting law complaint dated September 9th, 2026 to legal, unanimously.
Referred open meeting law complaint dated September 29th, 2026 to legal, unanimously.
Approved acceptance of a $27,999.02 bulletproof vest partnership award, unanimously.
Approved acceptance of $48,759.90 in state municipal road safety grant funds, unanimously.
Approved acceptance of a gift of equipment from Planet Fitness to the fire department, unanimously.
discussion: Arlington neighborhood sewer project: Residents asked for about $70 million to finish the remaining phases. The mayor put the remaining cost at about $88 million and said a joint letter to state and federal officials would follow.

School contract delays: Speakers said contracts sat in legal review for weeks, delaying software and equipment for students. The solicitor said the list of outstanding contracts was inaccurate and that many contracts reached legal after they expired.

Trash pickup and barrel fees: Members asked how to hold the trash vendor accountable for missed pickups and payment deductions under the contract. The mayor said 13 missed-pickup reports were filed in one week and bulk item pickup costs had grown.
Corruption investigation resolution: Public speakers urged the council to send the letter. Members debated whether to table the resolution, and a motion to table failed 4-4.

Echo Lane sewer betterment: The city has funds for a $450,000 sewer project on Echo Lane. Residents have concerns about paying back the cost through a betterment fee, and the mayor proposed a follow-up meeting with them.
